mainTopic: Whether an אמה העבריה goes free at her father's death (ריש לקיש is refuted), and who receives the הענקה, the parting gift for a freed Hebrew slave.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer: signs of maturity (סימנים) have a minimum age, and a ברייתא shows that hairs grown too early count only as a mole. Next the גמרא tests ריש לקיש's rule that an אמה העבריה goes free when her father dies. רב ששת challenges it from רבי שמעון's list of four ways of going free. The גמרא answers that the master's death is not on that list either, so the list holds only things with a set time. רב עמרם then brings a different ברייתא about the parting gift (הענקה). That list does include the master's death but leaves out the father's death, so ריש לקיש is refuted. His קל וחומר fails because signs change the girl's body and her father's death does not. Two ברייתות about who keeps the maidservant's gift are explained without helping ריש לקיש. Then the גמרא quotes the full ברייתא about the gift and its sources in the פסוקים. It closes by asking why a runaway gets no gift, since he must finish his six years anyway. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Signs of maturity have a lower limit
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the previous answer: סימנים have a fixed limit from below, a minimum age.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Signs do have a set limit] below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began just before. סימנים do have a fixed boundary 'below', meaning a minimum age before which they don't count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one can predict exactly when signs of maturity will show up. Still, there is an age below which they never count. This one word sets up the ברייתא that comes next as proof.

keyTerms.meaning: below; here, a minimum age
a fixed limit or set time
physical signs of maturity (two hairs)

phrases.english: Below.
phrases.notes: This finishes the line before it: signs of maturity have a set limit from below, meaning a minimum age.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סימנים have a fixed lower limit, a minimum age.

steps.title: Proof: hairs before a certain age are just a mole
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that two hairs grown at a young age don't count as a sign of maturity. This proves there is a lower limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: if a nine-year-old grows two hairs, it is a mole. From nine years and a day until twelve years and a day, even if the hairs stay, it is a mole. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it is a sign. At thirteen years and a day, everyone agrees it is a sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that signs of maturity have a minimum age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hairs at age nine are dismissed as a שומא (a mole), not a sign of maturity. Between nine and twelve, the תנא קמא still calls them a mole, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה counts them as a sign. At thirteen everyone agrees they count. Either way, there is clearly some age below which hairs mean nothing, and that is the 'lower limit'.

keyTerms.meaning: a mole; hairs growing from it don't count as maturity
and they are still on him
everyone agrees

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic age rules for when signs of maturity begin to count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says: it is a sign.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes רבי שמעון's list of four
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת challenges ריש לקיש with רבי שמעון's ברייתא. It counts exactly four ways of going free, three for a man and three for a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: רבי שמעון says there are four ways of going free where we give the slave a parting gift. Three apply to a man and three to a woman. You can't say all four apply to one person, because a man has no signs and a woman has no ear-piercing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a source to attack ריש לקיש's rule that an אמה העבריה goes free when her father dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון gives a numbered list of four ways of going free. Signs of maturity apply only to a woman, and רציעה (ear-piercing) applies only to a man. That is why each one has only three. Notice that the father's death is not on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: give a parting gift (הענקה) to a freed slave
piercing the ear of a slave who chooses to stay
for one person

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raises an objection:
Rabbi Shimon says:
in four cases we give them a parting gift,
three for a man, and three for a woman.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לוֹמַר אַרְבָּעָה בְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: And you cannot say four for one person,
because there are no signs for a man,
and there is no ear-piercing for a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב שֵׁשֶׁת

steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that an אמה העבריה goes free at her father's death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A numbered list from רבי שמעון leaves out the father's death.

steps.title: Why isn't the father's death on the list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the attack: if ריש לקיש is right, רבי שמעון should have listed the father's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: If ריש לקיש is right, let him also teach the father's death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what is bothering רב ששת about the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father's death really frees an אמה העבריה, it should appear among her ways of going free. It is missing, which suggests ריש לקיש is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: and if it were so
let him also teach
the father's death

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if ריש לקיש is right that her father's death sets her free.

phrases.english: let him also teach the father's death!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, נִיתְנֵי נָמֵי מִיתַת אָב

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something left out of a list suggests it isn't a real law.

steps.title: You can't say the תנא left things out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the usual answer that the תנא skipped some items, because he gave an exact number.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too the תנא taught some and left some out, but he says 'four'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shuts down a possible defense of ריש לקיש before anyone can use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we can answer 'תנא ושייר', meaning the תנא didn't list everything. But once a תנא gives an exact count, he is claiming the list is complete. So that answer doesn't work here.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא taught some and left some out
and if you would say

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי תַּנָּא וְשַׁיַּיר,
phrases.english: And if you say here too he taught and left out,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי תַּנָּא וְשַׁיַּיר

steps.title: You can't say he lists only things with a set time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a second defense: that the תנא lists only things with a fixed time. Signs have no fixed time, yet they are listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the תנא teaches things that have a set time and not things without a set time, but signs have no set time, and he teaches them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a second way out for ריש לקיש. The next step tries to rescue this defense using רב ספרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say the father's death was left out because no one knows when it will happen. But signs of maturity also have no exact date, and they are on the list. So that can't be the reason either.

keyTerms.meaning: something with a set time
but look

steps.whatToRemember: At this point 'he left things out' and 'he lists only things with a set time' have both been rejected. Steps 7–11 go on to answer רב ששת's challenge: the master's death is not one of the four, so the list holds only things with a set time.

phrases.english: And if you say the תנא teaches a matter that has a set time

steps.title: The fixed-time defense fails again: the master's death has no fixed time
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say signs do have a fixed time, following רב ספרא. But the death of the master has no fixed time at all, and it seems to be in the list anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too it follows רב ספרא, so signs do have a set time, there is still the death of the master. It has no set time, and yet the ברייתא teaches it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to rescue the 'fixed time' defense by using רב ספרא's view that signs have a minimum age. It then knocks that rescue down by pointing to the death of the master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said signs have no fixed time, so the list cannot be limited to fixed-time items. Using רב ספרא, the signs could count as having a fixed time after all. But the master's death can happen at any moment and still seems to be on the list, so the 'fixed time only' idea still falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (the גמרא brings up a possible answer)
Following the view of רב ספרא (that signs have a minimum age)
But there is still... (pointing to a problem)
The death of the master
A fixed, set time

phrases.english: And if you would say that here too
it follows רב ספרא,
phrases.notes: He means רב ספרא's idea that signs have a lower age limit, so they do have a kind of set time.

phrases.english: but there is still the death of the master,
which has no set time, and yet he teaches it!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letter in round brackets, so read it as לה: the master's death has no set time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי כִּדְרַב סָפְרָא, וְהָאִיכָּא מִיתַת אָדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to save the defense rejected in step 6, then rejects that attempt too.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבי שמעון's list only includes ways of going free that have a fixed time.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even if signs have a set time, the master's death has none, and it seems to be counted in the list.

steps.title: The master's death is not in the list either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא does not count the death of the master among its four ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: The death of the master is also not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last problem by saying we were wrong to think the master's death was one of the four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the master's death is not on the list, then everything on the list has a set time (once we use רב ספרא for signs). So it makes sense that the father's death, which has no set time, is also left out. That saves ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not teach it (it is not in the list)
Also, too

phrases.english: The death of the master is also not taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיתַת אָדוֹן נָמֵי לָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא: one item we assumed was on the list is not there.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the master's death was one of רבי שמעון's four ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: The master's death is not one of the four, so the list holds only fixed-time items, and leaving out the father's death is no problem.

steps.title: Then what are the four?
steps.stepSummary: If the master's death is not counted, the גמרא asks which four ways the ברייתא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what are the four?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple follow-up question that sets up the next step: name the four ways without the master's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the master's death off the list leaves a gap in the count of four. The גמרא must fill it, or the new reading does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: But then, if so

Four (the four ways of going free)

phrases.english: But then, what are the four?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which four ways of going free רבי שמעון counts, if the master's death is not one of them.

steps.title: The four: years, יובל, יובל after רציעה, and signs
steps.stepSummary: The four are: six years, יובל, יובל for a slave whose ear was pierced, and signs for an אמה העבריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Years, יובל, יובל of the pierced slave, and an אמה העבריה through signs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by naming the four ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man has three: years, יובל, and יובל after רציעה. A woman has three: years, יובל, and signs. That adds up to four different ways in total, three for each. This matches the ברייתא's count exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: The six years of service
The Jubilee year, when Hebrew slaves go free
Piercing the ear of a slave who wants to stay on
A Hebrew maidservant (a young girl)
Signs of physical maturity

phrases.english: Six years, and the Jubilee,

phrases.english: and a Hebrew maidservant through signs.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁנִים, וְיוֹבֵל, וְיוֹבֵל שֶׁל רְצִיעָה

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The four are: years, יובל, יובל after רציעה, and signs for an אמה העבריה. The master's death is not among them.

steps.title: Proof from the end of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא says no one person has all four ways. If the master's death counted, a woman would have four, so it must not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, because the end of the ברייתא teaches: You cannot say there are four for any one of them, because there are no signs for a man and no piercing for a woman. And if the master's death were counted, a woman at least would have four. Learn from this that it is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its new list with a proof from the last part of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the master's death on the list, a woman would have years, יובל, signs and the master's death, which makes four. But the ברייתא says no single person has four. So the master's death cannot be one of the four, just as step 8 said.

keyTerms.meaning: This also makes sense (a supporting proof is coming)
The last part of the teaching
You find it, there is such a case
Learn from this (the proof stands)

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי שמעון's ברייתא, the master's death is not one of the four ways. The end of the ברייתא proves this, and that removes רב ששת's challenge to ריש לקיש.

You cannot say

steps.raayaObject: That the master's death is not one of רבי שמעון's four ways.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the same ברייתא, which says no single person has all four ways.

steps.title: רב עמרם's challenge: the הענקה list leaves out the father's death
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the people who receive the parting gift. It includes the master's death and signs, but not the father's death. If ריש לקיש is right, it should list that too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם raises an objection: And these are the ones to whom we give a parting gift: one who leaves through years, through יובל, through the master's death, and an אמה העבריה through signs. And if ריש לקיש is right, let it also teach the father's death!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge against ריש לקיש begins, this time from a ברייתא about the הענקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the master's death clearly is listed, so the 'fixed time' answer cannot work. If an אמה העבריה goes free when her father dies, she should get the gift, and the ברייתא should say so.

keyTerms.meaning: They give the הענקה, the gift a freed slave receives
The death of the father

phrases.english: רב עמרם raises an objection:
And these are the ones to whom we give a parting gift:
one who leaves through the years, and through the Jubilee,
and through the death of the master,
and a Hebrew maidservant through signs.
And if it were so,
phrases.notes: He means: if ריש לקיש is right that she goes free when her father dies.

phrases.english: let it also teach the death of the father!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב עַמְרָם: וְאֵלּוּ מַעֲנִיקִים לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב ששת's challenge was answered, a new challenge comes from a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that an אמה העבריה goes free when her father dies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הענקה list includes the master's death, which has no set time, but leaves out the father's death. This suggests the father's death does not free her.

steps.title: The list is not incomplete, because it says 'these'
steps.stepSummary: The usual answer, that the תנא listed some cases and left others out, does not work here. The word 'these' shows a complete list.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say the תנא taught some and left some out, but it says 'these'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the easy answer to רב עמרם's challenge, so the challenge still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual answer is that a תנא sometimes leaves cases out. But opening with 'these' sounds like the full list and nothing more, much like the exact number did in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא taught some cases and left others out
'These', a word that suggests a complete list
But look, ... (pointing to a problem)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two lists. רבי שמעון's 'four ways' list does NOT include the master's death. The הענקה list does include it, so the 'fixed time' answer cannot help here.

phrases.english: And if you would say he taught some and left some out,
but he teaches 'these'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר, וְהָא אֵלּוּ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רב עמרם's challenge by blocking the easy answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The answer that the הענקה list is simply not complete.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא opens with 'these', which suggests a full and complete list.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that the list includes only ways with a fixed time
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say the ברייתא lists only ways of going free that come at a set time, and the father's death has no set time. But signs have no set time either, and they are listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the תנא lists only things that have a fixed time, and leaves out things without a fixed time, look at signs. They have no fixed time, and he still lists them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to explain why the father's death is missing from the ברייתא's list, and then knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed defense says the list includes only ways that happen at a predictable time, like six years or יובל, and the father's death is not predictable. But the list also includes סימנין, which come at no fixed time. So the reason fails.

steps.title: Even with רב ספרא's view, the master's death is still listed
steps.stepSummary: Someone might answer, using רב ספרא, that signs do have a kind of set time. But the master's death is also listed, and it certainly has no set time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too we follow רב ספרא, so signs do have a set time, there is still the master's death, which is listed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to save the fixed-time defense by using רב ספרא's view about signs, and then shows that the defense still fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רב ספרא, signs can be treated as having a set time, which would answer step 14. But the list also includes the master's death, and nobody can predict when a person will die. So the list clearly includes things without a fixed time, and the father's death should have been listed too.

keyTerms.meaning: The death of the master
But there is (points out a case that breaks the answer)

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי כִּדְרַב סָפְרָא,
phrases.english: And if you would say here too it is like רב ספרא,
phrases.notes: רב ספרא's view, said elsewhere, is that signs have a set time, so they would count as 'fixed'.

phrases.english: there is still the death of the master!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי כִּדְרַב סָפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repairs the defense from step 14 and then rejects it again.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the fixed-time defense even after using רב ספרא's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The master's death has no set time, yet it is listed.

steps.title: ריש לקיש is refuted
steps.stepSummary: With no defense left, the גמרא declares that ריש לקיש's view is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of ריש לקיש! It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up: no answer works, so ריש לקיש's view that the father's death frees her is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's list is complete, as step 13 showed, and it does not include the father's death. Every attempt to explain why it is missing has failed. So the ברייתא stands against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation that cannot be answered

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lists who gets the parting gift, and the list is complete. Since it leaves out the father's death, ריש לקיש is refuted.

phrases.english: A refutation of ריש לקיש!
It is a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge that started in step 12, now that every defense has failed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש's view, that the father's death frees an אמה העבריה from her master, is refuted.

steps.title: But ריש לקיש based his view on a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ריש לקיש can simply be refuted, since his view came from a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But ריש לקיש based his ruling on a קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: Even after the refutation, the גמרא asks what was wrong with ריש לקיש's reasoning. He had a logical argument, so where does it break?
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reasoned this way: signs free her from her master even though they do not fully free her from her father. Then the father's death, which does free her from her father, should surely free her from her master. The ברייתא shows his conclusion is wrong, but the גמרא wants to know the flaw in his logic.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument that if something holds in a weaker case, it surely holds in a stronger one
But surely (opens a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ קַל וָחוֹמֶר אָמַר!
phrases.english: But ריש לקיש said a קל וחומר!
phrases.notes: This points back to ריש לקיש's argument from earlier in the סוגיא, comparing signs with the father's death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ קַל וָחוֹמֶר אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the conclusion of step 16 by pointing to ריש לקיש's logical source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that ריש לקיש is refuted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר is a strong logical source. If no flaw is found in it, the refutation leaves his reasoning unexplained.

steps.title: The קל וחומר can be broken: signs change her body
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר fails because signs are special. They mean her body has changed, and the father's death does not change her body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The קל וחומר can be refuted, because one can argue: what makes signs special is that her body has changed. Can you say the same about the father's death, when her body has not changed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 17 by showing a weak point in ריש לקיש's קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר works only if the stronger case has everything the weaker case has. Signs have a special feature: her body has physically changed. The father's death does not have that feature. So we cannot learn the father's death from signs.

keyTerms.meaning: Refutable, able to be broken
To refute or break an argument
The body has changed
The death of the father

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule: a קל וחומר falls apart once you find a feature that only the source case has.

phrases.english: The קל וחומר is refutable,
because one can refute it:
what is special about signs is that the body has changed,
will you say the same about the father's death,
where the body has not changed?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר פְּרִיכָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר seemed solid, so ריש לקיש's view should stand.
steps.terutzMaskana: Signs have a special feature, a change in her body, that the father's death lacks. So the קל וחומר fails, and the refutation stands.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about who gets the maidservant's parting gift
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says the maidservant keeps her own parting gift. Another says her parting gift and her found items go to her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: a Hebrew slave's parting gift is his own, and a Hebrew maidservant's parting gift is her own. Another ברייתא teaches: a Hebrew maidservant's parting gift and the things she finds go to her father, and her master gets only payment for her lost work time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will try to resolve the contradiction in a way that helps ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא gives the maidservant's ענק to her. The second gives it to her father. These are two different rulings on the same gift, so they must be speaking about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The parting gift a master must give a Hebrew slave or maidservant when they go free
One ברייתא teaches
Lost items she finds
Payment for the work time that was lost

phrases.english: It is taught in one ברייתא:
the parting gift of a Hebrew slave is his own,
and the parting gift of a Hebrew maidservant is her own.
And it is taught in another ברייתא:
the parting gift of a Hebrew maidservant and what she finds belong to her father,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לְרַבָּה אֶלָּא שְׂכַר בַּטָּלָה בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: and her master has only payment for her lost time.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: עֶנֶק עֶבֶד עִבְרִי – לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ריש לקיש was refuted, the גמרא opens a new line that may support him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One ברייתא gives the maidservant's ענק to herself. Another gives it, along with her found items, to her father.

steps.title: Suggested resolution: one ברייתא is about signs, the other about the father's death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא that gives the gift to the father speaks about a girl freed by signs. The one that gives it to her speaks about a girl freed by her father's death, which would support ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not so that this one speaks about a girl who goes free through signs, and that one about a girl who goes free through her father's death?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to settle the two ברייתות in a way that would prove ריש לקיש right after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl freed by signs still has a living father, so her gift goes to him. A girl whose father died has no father to receive it, so she keeps it. This would mean the father's death is a way of going free, which is exactly ריש לקיש's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested proof)
That she goes out (goes free)

steps.confusionAlert: The order is reversed. The first 'הא' in this step points to the second ברייתא (the father gets it), and the second 'הא' points to the first ברייתא (she keeps it).

phrases.english: Is it not that
this one is where she goes out through signs,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא saying the gift goes to her father, since her father is still alive.

phrases.english: and that one is where she goes out through her father's death!
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא saying she keeps the gift herself, since she has no father anymore.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו, הָא – דְּנָפְקָא בְּסִימָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a way to settle the contradiction from step 19 that supports ריש לקיש.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that the father's death frees an אמה העבריה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two ברייתות about the ענק, read as one case of signs and one case of the father's death.

steps.title: Both ברייתות speak about a girl freed by signs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof for ריש לקיש. Both ברייתות speak about a girl freed by signs, and the difference is whether her father is still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Both ברייתות speak about a girl who went free through signs, and there is no contradiction. One speaks where the father is alive, and the other speaks where the father is no longer alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading from step 20 that gave ריש לקיש a proof. It offers a different way to explain why the two ברייתות disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the two ברייתות were split between two ways of going free: by signs, or by the father's death. Now both are placed in the same case, a girl freed by signs. If her father is alive, he takes the gift. If he has already died, she keeps it. Because of this, neither ברייתא speaks about a girl freed by her father's death, so ריש לקיש gets no support.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one
Physical signs of maturity
There is a father, meaning he is alive
There is no father, meaning he has died

phrases.english: No, both this one and that one
speak about where she went out through signs,
and it is not difficult:
this one is where there is a father,
that one is where there is no father.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אִידִי וְאִידִי דְּנָפְקָא לַהּ בְּסִימָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for ריש לקיש offered in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that one ברייתא speaks about a girl freed by her father's death.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two ברייתות can be split another way. Both speak about a girl freed by signs, and they differ over whether the father is alive, so no proof follows.

steps.title: Why the maidservant's ruling makes sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that saying the maidservant's gift is 'for herself' teaches something: it keeps her brothers from taking it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the ברייתא says a Hebrew maidservant's gift is for herself. This comes to exclude her brothers. As a ברייתא teaches: 'And you shall pass them down to your sons after you.' Them, meaning Canaanite slaves, go to your sons, but your daughters do not pass to your sons. From here we learn that a person does not pass down the rights he has to his daughter to his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question. It first agrees that one part of the ברייתא teaches something new, and then, in the next step, it will ask about another part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'בשלמא' means 'granted, this part makes sense.' The words 'for herself' teach that when the father dies, his rights in his daughter do not pass to his sons. That is learned from the פסוק about Canaanite slaves: only they are passed down as an inheritance, not daughters.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense (opens a contrast)
The parting gift given to a freed Hebrew servant
To exclude
Passes down as an inheritance
The rights a father has in his daughter

phrases.english: Granted, the parting gift of a Hebrew maidservant is for herself,
to exclude brothers,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And you shall pass them down to your sons after you"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:46. The פסוק is talking about Canaanite slaves.

phrases.english: them to your sons,
but not your daughters to your sons.
From here we learn that a person does not pass down
the rights to his daughter to his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא עֶנֶק אָמָה הָעִבְרִיָּה לְעַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that both ברייתות are explained, the גמרא looks closely at the wording of the ברייתא that says the gift is 'for herself.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'for himself / for herself' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the first half of the question: the maidservant's wording is justified, which sets up the contrast with the slave.

steps.title: A Hebrew slave's gift is obviously his
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to say a Hebrew slave's gift is for himself. Who else could get it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But that the gift of a Hebrew slave is for himself, that is obvious! To whom else would it go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks its real question. Saying a male Hebrew slave keeps his own gift seems to teach nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the maidservant, someone else might have a claim, such as her father or her brothers. A male slave has nobody who owns his rights like that, so 'for himself' looks like an empty statement.

keyTerms.meaning: A Hebrew slave
It is obvious
To whom?

phrases.english: But the parting gift of a Hebrew slave is for himself,
that is obvious! Rather, to whom else?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא עֶנֶק עֶבֶד עִבְרִי לְעַצְמוֹ – פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'בשלמא... אלא' question begun in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a Hebrew slave's gift is for himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A statement in a ברייתא should teach something. This one seems to teach nothing, because no one else could claim the slave's gift.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a small point made big
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף admits the statement teaches nothing new. The ברייתא just made a big statement out of a small point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I see a י made into a city here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question by agreeing that the statement is not needed. The ברייתא said it anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of finding a hidden lesson, רב יוסף accepts that the words about the male slave add nothing. The ברייתא simply said it anyway, even though it teaches nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter י, the smallest letter
A city
I see

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
I see a yod made into a city here.
phrases.notes: A saying: something as tiny as the letter י has been blown up as big as a city. Here, a point that needs no saying was said anyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹד קֶרֶת קָא חָזֵינָא הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts that the wording is unneeded and explains it as style
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every phrase in the ברייתא must teach a new law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase about the male slave is not needed. It was said without adding a new law.

steps.title: אביי for רב ששת: the ברייתא follows תוטאי
steps.stepSummary: אביי, quoting רב ששת, says the ברייתא follows תוטאי, who teaches that the slave's gift is his and not his creditor's.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what רב ששת said. Whose view is this ברייתא? It is תוטאי. As a ברייתא teaches, תוטאי says: 'To him,' and not to his creditor.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second answer, and this one finds real meaning in the words 'for himself.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is someone who might take the slave's gift: a person the slave owes money to. תוטאי learns from the word 'to him' in the פסוק that the creditor cannot collect it, and the ברייתא's 'for himself' teaches that same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
A תנא who taught this ruling
His creditor, someone he owes money to

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why the ברייתא says a Hebrew slave's gift is 'for himself.' רב יוסף says the words add nothing. רב ששת says they teach, like תוטאי, that the slave's creditor cannot take the gift.
steps.whyThisMatters: תוטאי's rule shows that the parting gift is meant to reach the freed slave himself, so it is kept safe even from his creditors.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: אביי said: This is what רב ששת said:
Whose view is this? It is תוטאי.
As it is taught in a ברייתא, תוטאי says:
"To him," and not to his creditor.
phrases.notes: דברים 15:14.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָא מַנִּי – תּוּטַאי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 23 than רב יוסף did.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the ברייתא to a specific תנא, which gives the wording a real purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No one but the slave could claim his gift, so 'for himself' is empty.
steps.terutzMaskana: A creditor might claim it. 'For himself' teaches, like תוטאי, that the creditor cannot.

steps.title: The full list of who gets a severance gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the full ברייתא. Those freed by six years, the יובל, the master's death, or סימנים get a gift. The runaway and the one who leaves by גרעון כסף do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the ברייתא itself: These get a severance gift: one who goes free after his years, at the יובל, or when the master dies, and a Hebrew maidservant who goes free through signs of growing up. But a runaway, and one who leaves by paying off the rest of his time, do not get a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes, word for word, the ברייתא it was using earlier. This opens a new section about the ברייתא's own rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes two lists. The first list is the ways a slave goes free by himself, through time or events. The second list is a runaway and a slave who pays his way out, and they get no gift.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself.' The גמרא returns to look at a source it quoted earlier
They give the severance gift (הַעֲנָקָה) to a freed slave
The Jubilee year, when all Hebrew slaves go free
Physical signs of growing up. They free a Hebrew maidservant
A runaway slave
Paying off the rest of the slave's time to go free early

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to study the ברייתא it quoted earlier.

phrases.english: These are the ones to whom one gives a severance gift:
one who goes free through years,
and through the Jubilee, and through the master's death,
and a Hebrew maidservant through signs of maturity.
But a runaway, and one who goes free by deducting money,
one does not give him a severance gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אֵלּוּ מַעֲנִיקִים לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the earlier discussion and quotes in full the ברייתא that was used in it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaves freed by years, יובל, master's death, or סימנים get הענקה. A runaway and one freed by גרעון כסף do not.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the one who buys himself out does get a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר agrees that the runaway gets nothing. He holds that the one who leaves by גרעון כסף does get a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: A runaway does not get a gift, but one who goes free by paying off his time does get a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר disagrees with the first opinion about only one case: the slave who pays his way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree about the runaway. The only disagreement is the slave who pays off his remaining time. For רבי מאיר, that slave moves into the group that gets a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: They give him the gift

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
A runaway, one does not give him a gift,
but one who goes free by deducting money, one does give him a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion inside the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A runaway gets no הענקה. One freed by גרעון כסף does get הענקה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון counts four ways of going free
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says there are four ways of going free that bring a gift. Three of them apply to a man and three apply to a woman, because סימנים are only for a woman and רציעה is only for a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: There are four ways, and those who go free by them get a gift. Three apply to a man and three apply to a woman. You cannot say all four apply to one person, because a man does not go free by signs and a woman is not pierced.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds a way of counting the cases. This ends the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He explains why no single person can have all four ways. One way, סימנים, is only for a woman. Another, רציעה, is only for a man. So each person has only three.

keyTerms.meaning: Piercing the ear of a slave who wants to stay. It applies only to a man

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
There are four, and one gives them a severance gift,
three for a man and three for a woman,
and you cannot say
that all four apply to one of them
because there are no signs for a man
and no piercing for a woman.
phrases.notes: The word 'no' carries over from the line before: there is also no piercing for a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַרְבָּעָה מַעֲנִיקִים לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third voice in the same ברייתא that organizes the cases by counting them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four ways of going free that bring הענקה. Three apply to each gender, since סימנים are only for a woman and רציעה is only for a man.

steps.title: What is the source for these rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the תורה these rules about the gift come from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the פסוק behind the ברייתא's lists. This sets up the next step, which brings the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave rules but no source. The גמרא wants to know which words of the תורה include some slaves and leave out others.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where are these things?' A request for the source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches which freed slaves get הענקה

steps.title: The extra 'send him' includes the other ways of going free
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the words 'תשלחנו' and 'וכי תשלחנו' widen the gift. Not only the six-year slave gets it, but also the one freed by יובל, the master's death, or סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: I might think only one who goes free after six years gets a gift. From where do we include one who goes free at the יובל, at the master's death, and an אמה העבריה through signs? The פסוק says 'send him' and 'and when you send him'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It uses the double mention of 'sending' in the פסוק to include more cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the gift is written about the six-year slave. The extra mention of 'sending' teaches that anyone who is sent free in these ways also gets the gift.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall send him' away free
To include more cases
'The פסוק teaches.' This brings the proof text

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
One might think that one gives a severance gift
only to one who goes free after six years.
From where do we include one who goes free in the Jubilee,
and one freed through the master's death,
and a Hebrew maidservant who goes free through signs?
The verse states: 'send him' and 'and when you send him.'
phrases.notes: דברים 15:13. 'Sending' shows up twice in that פסוק, and the extra one adds the other cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהוּ מַעֲנִיקִים אֶלָּא לַיּוֹצֵא בְּשֵׁשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The double language of 'sending' in the פסוק includes יובל, the master's death, and סימנים

steps.title: 'From you' leaves out the runaway and the one who buys himself out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The words 'חפשי מעמך' mean the master sends him. That leaves out the runaway and the one who leaves by גרעון כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Might I include a runaway and one who goes free by paying off his time? The פסוק says 'and when you send him free from you': only one whose sending is from you. That leaves out the runaway and the one who pays his way out, since their sending is not from you.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now limits the rule. It uses the words 'from you' to leave out the cases that get no gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a slave whose going free comes from the master's side gets the gift. The runaway leaves on his own. This first opinion holds that the one who pays his way out is also not 'sent by you'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Free from you.' The words that limit the gift
His being sent away
'Is excluded.' Left out of the rule

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'יצא' does not mean the slave 'went out' free. It is a learning word meaning 'this case is left out' of the rule.

phrases.english: One might think that I include
a runaway and one who goes free by deducting money?
The verse states: 'And when you send him free from you,'
phrases.notes: דברים 15:13

phrases.english: meaning one whose sending is from you,
which excludes a runaway and one who goes free by deducting money,
whose sending is not from you.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה בּוֹרֵחַ וְיוֹצֵא בְּגִרְעוֹן כֶּסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on the rule that the previous step widened
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מעמך' limits the gift to slaves sent by the master, so the runaway and the one freed by גרעון כסף are left out

steps.title: רבי מאיר: paying out is still 'sent from you'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reads 'מעמך' the same way. He holds that the slave who leaves by גרעון כסף is sent by the master, so only the runaway is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: A runaway does not get a gift, since his sending is not from you. But one who goes free by paying off his time is sent from you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר uses the same words, 'from you'. He applies them differently to the slave who pays his way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree on the test: is the slave sent by the master? They disagree only about whether paying off the time counts as being sent by the master. For רבי מאיר it does, so that slave gets a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since there is not.' This gives the reason

steps.whatToRemember: The test for the severance gift is 'מעמך': was the slave sent off by the master? Everyone agrees the runaway fails this test. רבי מאיר holds that the slave who pays his way out passes it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
A runaway, one does not give him a gift,
since his sending is not from you,
but one who goes free by deducting money,
his sending is from you.
phrases.notes: The ending is left unsaid: so he does get the gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: בּוֹרֵחַ אֵין מַעֲנִיקִין לוֹ, דְּאֵין שִׁילּוּחוֹ מֵעִמָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי מאיר's opinion from step 27, using the same words of the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave freed by גרעון כסף counts as 'sent from you' and gets הענקה. A runaway does not.

steps.title: But the runaway has to finish his years anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא that left out the runaway slave. A בורח must make up the years he missed, so in the end he does go free after full service.
steps.simpleTranslation: A runaway slave needs to complete his years!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ברייתא from Step 31, which said the runaway gets no gift. It points out that a runaway still has to come back and finish his time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treated the בורח as someone who leaves without the master sending him. But if he must come back and complete his six years, then in the end he leaves after full service, just like a regular slave. So why should he be left out of the gift?

keyTerms.meaning: A runaway, a slave who escapes from his master
Completing, making up the time that was missed
Needs, is required to

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking whether running away is allowed. It is saying that running away does not end his service, because he still owes the missing years.

phrases.english: A runaway – he needs to complete [his years]!

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹרֵחַ – הַשְׁלָמָה בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exclusion of the runaway made in Steps 31 and 32 (both the ברייתא and רבי מאיר leave him out).
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that 'חפשי מעמך' excludes the בורח from the gift
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A runaway must make up his missing years. After he completes them he leaves after full service like a regular slave, so he should get the gift too.

steps.title: Proof that a runaway must finish his six years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that a בורח must complete his term. It learns this from the פסוק 'שש שנים יעבד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that a runaway must complete his years? The פסוק says, 'Six years he shall work.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a ברייתא. The ברייתא proves that a runaway must finish his six years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the slave works 'six years', which means a full six years and no less. So time spent running away does not count, and he has to make it up. This makes the challenge stronger: the runaway really does finish his full service, so why does he lose the gift?

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)
The פסוק teaches

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the problem the גמרא now has to solve: what is the ברייתא's 'runaway' who gets no gift, if every runaway must finish his years anyway?

phrases.english: As it is taught: From where [do we know] about a runaway
that he is obligated to complete [his years]?
The verse states: "Six years he shall work."
phrases.notes: שמות 21:2
